title: Red Hat Security Advisory: bubblewrap security update
description: A security vulnerability (CVE-2026-87766) affects bubblewrap, a core execution engine for unprivileged containers used as a setuid binary on kernels without user namespaces. The flaw involves a symlink traversal via /oldroot that allows writing files outside the intended sandbox during setup. Red Hat has issued an important security update for bubblewrap in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 Extended Update Support and related variants to address this issue.
aiSummary: Bubblewrap (/usr/bin/bwrap) is a setuid binary used as a core execution engine for unprivileged containers on kernels lacking user namespaces. The vulnerability CVE-2026-87766 is a symlink traversal flaw via /oldroot that permits an attacker to write files outside the sandbox during the container setup phase. This could potentially allow unauthorized modification of files on the host system. Red Hat has released an update for bubblewrap in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 Extended Update Support and related product variants to fix this issue.
aiImpact: The vulnerability allows writing files outside the sandbox during setup, which could lead to unauthorized file modifications on the host system. This compromises the isolation guarantees provided by bubblewrap containers, potentially enabling privilege escalation or host system compromise. The severity is rated as important by Red Hat Product Security.
